To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
progesterone receptors mediate cervical remodeling at term and loss of their actions induces premature cervical ripening, which is associated with preterm birth.

the cervix of rats treated with progesterone receptor antagonists or ovariectimized on day 17 of pregnancy is characterized by a reduced density of cell nuclei and collagen content, as well as an increased number of macrophages, similar to the cervix of pregnant rats at term.

progesterone receptor antagonists induce preterm cellular and structural remodeling of the rat cervix that is similar to that observed at term, while ovariectomy-induced preterm birth is not associated with changes in the structure or macrophage census of the cervix.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms that control the timing of birth and how these mechanisms are perturbed in preterm birth.
the mechanisms by which the cervix is remodeled in preparation for parturition.
the cellular mechanisms that regulate the structural remodeling of the uterine cervix and the onset of labor at term and preterm birth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
progesterone receptor actions are essential for the maintenance of the cervix at a preparturient stage, and that the loss of these actions promotes preterm birth.
the cervix is remodeled at parturition at both preterm and term and the mechanisms of remodeling are similar.
the cervix undergoes structural and cellular remodeling at term and that the loss of nuclear progestin receptor-mediated actions is associated with premature remodeling of the cervical structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
loss of progesteronereceptor actions in the cervix results in a preterm cervical phenotype that is similar to that found at term.
the preterm cervicovaginal remodelling induced by the loss of progrestone receptor actions in the cervix is similar to the remodelling of the cervix at parturition.

the loss of progsterone receptor-mediated actions, whether by progesterone receptor antagonism or ovariectomy, induces preterm cellular and structural remodeling of the rat cervix and premature birth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
loss of progesteronemediated actions promotes preterm cervical remodeling and birth.
loss of progesteronemediated actions in the cervix is associated with preterm labor and delivery.
progesterone receptors are necessary for the maintenance of the structural and cellular properties of the cervix.
